ab_adams_lake_wall_wonderous_wanderer.descent_text: Rappel the route down its own anchors.

ab_dune_wall_stilgars_corner.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belay stations, which have rings.

ab_first_wall_lower_ramp.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right of the wall, or rappel from the sport and trad anchors to the base.

ab_grey_ghost_wall_bonanza.approach: Start from the Devil's Gap trailhead in the Lake Minnewanka valley and follow the steep trail up to the base of Grey Ghost Wall, a south-facing wall.

ab_lady_macdonald_east_south_east_ridge.descent_text: After joining the Lady Macdonald scramble on the summit ridge, follow the hiker's scramble trail down to where Cougar Creek begins.

ab_medicine_slab_the_nutcracker_ball_aka.descent_text: Rappel the route; traverse back across the big ledge to reach the anchors for the first two pitches.

ab_roche_a_perdrix_chimney_route.descent_text: Rappel from the Metolius rap hangers on the route, or scramble up to the summit and follow the scramble route down.

ab_vacation_wall_limestone_vacation.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted belays.

ab_upper_norquay_slab_calamari_crack.approach: The slab is reached from a pullout on the westbound Trans-Canada Highway, roughly midway between the Mount Norquay turnoff and the Bow Valley Parkway turnoff. Cross the animal fence at the runoff channel and follow the channel a short way, then climb the ridge on its right under the power lines and through burned timber, picking up a faint trail to the crest. Follow the crest past flat spots and rock steps; where the ridge dips to a col and then steepens, take the trail round to the right and onto the ridge again. A slab blocks the ridge at the next flat spot, so drop down and left past a cairn, cross a stand of trees and a wide scree-filled gully, staying left of it (ignore the trail that heads up to a rock step). Follow the downhill trail to the edge of a cliff, which is the top of the lower slab, turn right along it to an opening, and the upper slab lies straight ahead. The route climbs the corner immediately to the right of Escargot Corner.

ab_upper_norquay_slab_escargot_corner.descent_text: From the top-out ledge walk up and left, then up and right onto the ridge system. Follow the ridge down to a sharp drop, where a boulder wrapped in a black chain serves as the rappel anchor. Rappel to easier ground, then scramble down the ridge to rejoin the approach trail.
ab_upper_norquay_slab_escargot_corner.approach: The slab is reached from a pullout on the westbound Trans-Canada Highway, roughly midway between the Mount Norquay turnoff and the Bow Valley Parkway turnoff. Cross the animal fence at the runoff channel and follow the channel a short way, then climb the ridge on its right under the power lines and through burned timber, picking up a faint trail to the crest. Follow the crest past flat spots and rock steps; where the ridge dips to a col and then steepens, take the trail round to the right and onto the ridge again. A slab blocks the ridge at the next flat spot, so drop down and left past a cairn, cross a stand of trees and a wide scree-filled gully, staying left of it (ignore the trail that heads up to a rock step). Follow the downhill trail to the edge of a cliff, which is the top of the lower slab, turn right along it to an opening, and the upper slab lies straight ahead. Escargot Corner is the first right-facing corner counting from the left side of the upper slab.

ak_5390_west_face_granitic_dreams.descent_text: Walk off to the south over the snow, the same way as the other west face routes. Rappelling the route is not advised, because it is long.

ak_crown_jewel_crown_royal.descent_text: Rappel the route rather than downclimbing the snow and crossing the bergschrund again.

ak_devil_s_thumb_south_pillar_free.descent_text: Descend the route by rappel, using the face below the traverse until you re-enter the large corner system.

ak_gunnysack_creek_stairway_to_heaven.descent_text: Walk off by bushwhacking across to the neighbouring hill, then take the trails back down to Gunnysack.

ak_main_wall_moon_pilot.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel over the large roof from the separate two-bolt anchor that belongs to a different route.

ak_main_wall_2_birthday_on_the_sheep_tra.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right, down toward the East Tower and back to camp.

ak_new_harbor_harbor_fever.descent_text: Rappel off the alders, or walk off along the main trail.

ak_southeast_buttress_barnyard_betty.descent_text: After the last pitch, untie, walk to the true summit, and descend to the right into the amphitheatre; it returns you to the base of the climb.

ak_the_throne_oxidado_express.descent_text: From the west summit, go down The Lost Marsupial route on the formation's south side to reach the glacier.

ak_razorback_razorbutt.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Razorback is a small cragging spot between the Southeast Buttress and the East Tower: hike up and right of the buttress to just below the tower, with the lines on the formation's right-hand side as seen when walking up. Razorbutt is a wide crack on the formation's rear face; climb the slope and curl behind the rock to find it.

ak_southeast_buttress_homewrecker.descent_text: From the anchor behind the summit tower, rappel into the gully. Downclimb fourth-class ground to a big boulder with slings beneath it, then rappel again to the floor of the Keyhole.
ak_southeast_buttress_homewrecker.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Southeast Buttress is the feature on the right side of the main wall. Homewrecker takes the prominent dihedral that arcs leftward near the middle of the buttress; the first pitch starts up a low-angle grassy gully at the middle of the buttress toe, which most parties scramble.

ak_spirit_boulder_area_cali_slit.approach: From Palmer, take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then the gravel Archangel Road, and follow it past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing and bouldering in the basin begins. Spirit Boulder Area lies left of the approach gully that serves Shield, Main Wall and Two Toke Tower, and Cali Slit is left of the Spirit Boulder chalice. It slabs past two bolts into a roof, then crosses the lip into a left-trending slit.

ak_weird_alaska_wall_unnamed_4.approach: Heading out from Haines, park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch and follow the creek past the culvert to a flagged trail into the woods, which leads to a boulder field. A trail runs up the right side of the boulder field to the main wall, arriving at the base of Chest Fur, with the routes lying to its right. Unnamed 4 is the obvious overhanging crack as you move right along the wall.

az_little_leviathan_zig_zag.descent_text: Bolted anchors at the top are used to get down.

bc_3_south_west_faces_from_adamant_or_au.descent_text: Rappel the route, since fixed tat marks every belay, or hike down from the summit on its west side and circle back to the Austerity Glacier.

bc_crow_s_nest_alcove_faith_healer.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.

bc_goat_lake_area_patio_seating.descent_text: The top is a broad grassy flat. Short rappels lead directly back to the pass on Denture Ridge; look for the anchors made of pins, nuts and cord.

bc_grimface_grimface_se_chimney.descent_text: The usual descent is down the west ridge.

bc_grimface_matriarch_sw_face.descent_text: Continue along the Matriarch-Macabre-Grimface traverse and come down Grimface's west ridge to return to the meadow.

bc_grimface_se_notch.descent_text: Walk off to the northwest; cairns mark the easiest way down.

bc_hermit_narrows_baby_alpine.descent_text: After the finish, scramble up and over slabs to an alpine lake, then hike back down into the grassy gully at the foot of the wall.

bc_hermit_narrows_screams_across_the_val.descent_text: Rappel the route, or walk off either side.

bc_joint_wall_above_all_splendour.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at either belay.

bc_middle_hidden_walls_hidden_treasure.descent_text: Walk off from the bolted anchor, or rappel from the separate anchor to the left.

bc_middle_hidden_walls_stuck_in_the_midd.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.

bc_middle_hidden_walls_vicious_bastard.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.

bc_mouses_tooth_mighty_mouse.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Bolted anchors are on every pitch but the fourth.

bc_pigeon_feathers_electric_funeral.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Not every rappel anchor sits at a belay, so note them on the way up; the anchors may need fresh cord.

bc_pigeon_feathers_fingerberry_jam.descent_text: Descend by rappel; some of the rappels are long enough that a tag line is needed.

bc_pigeon_feathers_furry_friends.descent_text: Use two ropes to rappel from the bolted stations down the spire's west face.

bc_pigeon_feathers_gravy_train.descent_text: Every belay is equipped with rappel hangers, so the route can be rappelled.

bc_pigeon_feathers_solitary_confinement.descent_text: The anchors are bolted, so the route can be rappelled with two ropes.

bc_tantalus_tantalus_standard_route.approach: The approach to Tantalus crosses the Dione Glacier from the hut, and the climb needs a screw or a picket for the bergschrund.

bc_the_old_settler_totally_spurious.descent_text: Come down the south peak's south ridge, the way used from the West Buttress.

bc_west_ear_helix.approach: Come up the gully from the Gimli main trail; the West Ear is on the looker's left. Helix starts on the left side of the ear on grassy ledges.
bc_west_ear_helix.descent_text: Descend the gully to the left of the route. It is also the bail-out line, reached by traversing left.

bc_west_ear_the_pack.descent_text: Rappel the route on the bolted stations, which have been updated. It is possible to rappel from near the top of the fourth pitch.

bc_the_deacon_sentinel_direct.approach: Reach the meadow camp below the Deacon, then climb to the Deacon-Matriarch col and traverse the ridgeline toward the Deacon. Drop onto snow and talus to reach the foot of the northeast face. Both lines begin beneath a big V-shaped feature at the climber's-left (east) end of the face. Sentinel Direct climbs the left fork of the V.

bc_the_deacon_the_heretic.approach: Reach the meadow camp below the Deacon, then climb to the Deacon-Matriarch col and traverse the ridgeline toward the Deacon. Drop onto snow and talus to reach the foot of the northeast face. Both lines begin beneath a big V-shaped feature at the climber's-left (east) end of the face. The Heretic takes the right fork, an undercling ramp slanting up and right.
bc_the_deacon_the_heretic.descent_text: Gain the ridge above the route and drop off it ahead of the loose, blocky towers. One rappel is followed by a traverse over looser but lower-angle, less exposed rock to the summit. Then walk the ridgeline down; cornices build over the gullies beside it, so avoid cutting across snow early in the season.

bc_vowell_group_archduke_trio.approach: Start on the lower Vowell Glacier, work up into the cirque, and bear right to the beginning of the route. The route begins on the right (east-northeast) side with easy scrambling to where the technical climbing starts, then follows the knife-edge ridge over three summits.
bc_vowell_group_archduke_trio.descent_text: From the third summit, rappel the ridgeline down to the glacier. Fixed rappel anchors are not to be expected, so bring slings for spikes and boulders.

ca_bubbs_creek_wall_hanshi.descent_text: Rappel from the top down to the level where Hanshi joins What's Up Bubb, then follow that route's rappels to the base.

nm_mummy_the_route_1.descent_text: Descent is a rappel down the south face along the line of ascent, from anchors on the summit.

nm_sentinel_east_osa.descent_text: The back side of the formation is a walk-off.

nv_the_snags_fawn_arete.descent_text: Walk off the back of the tower from the top.

co_sharkstooth_northeast_ridge.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead and walk toward Loch Vale. At the Andrews Glacier junction, which is easy to miss, keep low in the valley beside the glacial runoff rather than following the trail up toward the glacier; that lower line avoids the worst of the boulders on the way to the Gash. Hike up the Gash, the large boulderfield below the rock, and as you near the spire a long fin of rock comes off the northeast ridge. Climb to the east of that fin and scramble up large ledges to start.
co_sharkstooth_northeast_ridge.descent_text: From the summit, cairns lead down a small gully to the southeast to bolted rappel anchors. A few rappels reach the top of the Gash, with a class 3 downclimb after the last one, and the Gash takes you down to the trail.

co_the_crestones_the_prow_kit_carson.approach: The route can be reached from the Spanish Creek, Willow Lakes or South Colony Lakes trailheads. The Spanish Creek approach crosses private monastery land and needs a permit arranged ahead. The Prow is the fin on the southwest ridge of Kit Carson Mountain, of Crestone conglomerate. Scramble third class to the base of the fin, and the first move up a bulge begins the route.
co_the_crestones_the_prow_kit_carson.descent_text: Head east a long way, going over another peak, to the wide valley in the saddle separating Kit Carson from Ellingwood, which allows a return to camp. Cutting back early leads onto steep slabs.

id_pillar_pandemicas_pillar_pandemicas.descent_text: Rappel from the single-bolt anchor on top, then continue down from the notch anchor.

mt_white_wall_the_kids_with_guns.descent_text: All anchors are bolted, so the route can be rappelled, or you can walk off toward the Tick Farm area.

or_bridge_group_the_the_newt_route.descent_text: Cross back over the bridge from the summit and scramble down to the saddle on the uphill side.

ut_devil_s_castle_enemy_at_the_gate.descent_text: Walk off. Routes on the Castle are normally walked off.

ut_devil_s_castle_poon_limp_or_eat_crust.descent_text: Rappel the route from the belay anchors.

ut_devil_s_castle_touch_of_grey.descent_text: Walk off. Routes on the Castle are normally walked off.

wy_warrior_1_east_face_left.descent_text: Cross the top of the tower to the rappel route that goes down the Northeast Face.

wy_warrior_1_northeast_face_r_of_warrior.descent_text: Rappel down climber's left of the route.

wy_wolfs_head_fred_beckey_s_route.descent_text: Rappel the route from natural anchors and sling stations. Take care when pulling the ropes, as there are loose blocks and flakes where the rope can stick.
wy_wolfs_head_fred_beckey_s_route.approach: Approach the cirque from the Big Sandy trailhead and follow the trail along the west side past Pingora into the cirque lake basin. Take the Wolf's Head trail where it splits from the south side of Pingora to a slabby, flowery ramp, and follow it along the base of Wolf's Head, with some fourth-class traversing, to the foot of the route, directly below the thumb-like spire.
